patch.value:
## Scope, from the live audit
Four legacy codes on terminal items only: ninety-eight retired no-active-blocker sentinel references; eight duplicated relationship spellings between terminal endpoints; eight terminal-only ordering cycles spanning forty-nine items, the largest across twenty-three closed milestone items; three dangling references to absent targets.

## Why this needs to be a batch and not opportunistic cleanup
Touching a closed item updates its timestamp, and the changelog buckets by that timestamp — so ad hoc repair silently drags years-old closed work into the current release notes. Doing all of it at once, deliberately, with the changelog effect measured and regenerated as the final step, is the only safe shape.

## Method
Read-only classification first, producing the full edge list per code. Then a single mutation batch. Then changelog regeneration and an explicit statement of which buckets moved and why. Never mutate a closed item outside this batch.

## Boundary
Removal of meaningless edges only. This wave adds no new relationships — enrichment is the separate active and terminal backfill waves.
Graph wave: changelog-safe legacy edge hygiene batch — retire the no-active-blocker sentinel, duplicate spellings, terminal ordering cycles, and dangling terminal references

The no-active-blocker sentinel references are removed from all holders; blocker state derives from real edges only; Duplicated parent and child spellings between terminal endpoints collapse to the canonical single spelling; Terminal-only ordering cycles are broken by dropping the single lowest-evidence edge per cycle, with the choice recorded; Dangling terminal references to absent items are resolved or removed with the rationale recorded on the holder; The changelog effect is measured before and after; regeneration runs as the last step and any bucket movement is stated explicitly in the batch record; pm graph audit reports zero findings for all four legacy codes after the batch
The audit reports zero legacy findings without dragging closed items into a release changelog

One hundred and fifty-eight terminal items carry edges that mean nothing: a retired sentinel, duplicated parent and child spellings of the same relationship, ordering cycles between closed milestones, and references to items that never existed. Every graph traversal and every audit run pays to skip them.
Removes the permanent noise floor from graph governance so that a non-zero audit finding count becomes actionable again instead of expected.
The audit's four legacy codes report zero, executed as one deliberate batch whose changelog effect is controlled and stated up front.
The audit itself names the remediation as a dedicated changelog-safe closed-item batch and explicitly forbids ad hoc repair. That batch has never been scheduled, so the findings recur on every run.

value.text:
Batch executed for three of four codes, changelog effect measured first rather than assumed.

Before: 11 findings; nodes 2458 (missing_nodes 3); edges 12116; tracker-context-quality verdict pass.

Executed:
- legacy_duplicate_edge 8 -> 0. Collapsed 8 reciprocal child rows onto the canonical parent edge each child already stored: pm-7t04 (5 rows: 0nia, 1265, 8rjn, b8rf, g2nd) and pm-v7dj (3 rows: aqat, jauk, ze5g). Lossless, because parent and child are declared inverses and every child stores the parent spelling.
- missing_reference_terminal 3 -> 0. Removed pm-1p2u's related row to the non-existent pm-0wm0, and cleared two legacy free-text blocked_by scalars that were never item ids (pm-lty 'backlog-sequencing', pm-zdec 'design-review').
- legacy_no_blocker_sentinel 98 -> 0. Cleared the retired no-active-blocker scalar on all 98 holders; blocker state now derives from real edges only.

After: 8 findings, all legacy_ordering_cycle; nodes 2455; edges 12105.

Changelog effect, measured not assumed: regeneration diff was 15 lines, all intra-section reordering of the four touched closed items within their own already-published release sections. No item entered [Unreleased]; no section gained or lost an item. All 98 sentinel holders and all 4 touched items carry a release value, which is the field the generator buckets by. Filed as pm-71v4l9: the closed_at rule this item's body relies on over-counts the risky population by 4.4x (1475 vs the real 337).

Fourth code not executed, and it is not a scheduling choice: the root cause of all 8 cycles is now known (26 holders storing a scalar blocked_by X together with a contradicting structured row X,blocks; full list on pm-xvt7ps), the repair is mechanical, and removing those 26 rows takes edges to 12079 against graph-edges-floor 12103 at block enforcement. Recorded blocked_by pm-mfvsng.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
CI hardening attempted and blocked, recorded so the earned state is not mistaken for an enforced one.

The three ceilings this batch drove to zero are still declared at their pre-batch values: graph-finding-legacy-duplicate-edge-ceiling 8, graph-finding-legacy-no-blocker-sentinel-ceiling 98, graph-finding-missing-reference-terminal-ceiling 3. Tightening them to 0 is what converts this batch from a one-off cleanup into a regression gate, and it is the whole reason the batch is worth doing.

Every attempt fails: 'Workspace history state for assurance.json changed outside the audited mutation path.' The refusal is correct and predates this session — the committed registry carries two loosenings that the append-only workspace stream never recorded (health-telemetry-zero block to warn, graph-outcome-reachable-floor 2438 to 2434), both written by commit 0132ed74b. Filed as pm-h06944 with the full replay diff. Until it is reconciled the assurance registry is frozen for all writes, including no-op re-puts.

So the batch's state is: three of four legacy codes cleaned to zero in the data, zero of three earned ceilings tightened in the declarations. A regression that re-introduces sentinels, duplicate parent/child spellings or dangling references would still pass CI today. This item should not close until the ceilings are at 0, which makes it dependent on pm-h06944 as well as pm-mfvsng.
